name: application-terminal-command-palette
title: Terminal Command Palette
description: Inline command runner styled like a terminal: a scrollable history of prior command/output pairs colored by outcome, above a live input line with a blinking caret.
useWhen: Building an in-app admin console or debug panel where users type and run real commands against your system.
You need to show command output (success, error, or informational) inline in a running history, not just a single result.
Distinct from Terminal Blocks (a static code/output display) and Command (a fuzzy-search action palette) — this component actually accepts and runs typed input.
avoidWhen: You only need to display a static, non-interactive terminal transcript — use Terminal Blocks instead.
Users are searching/selecting from a fixed list of actions rather than typing free-form commands — use the Command component instead.
responsiveBehavior: The history pane has a fixed max-height and scrolls internally; the panel itself is a fixed-width block that doesn't reflow its monospace layout at narrower widths.
accessibility: The history region carries role="log" and aria-live="polite" so new command/output pairs are announced as they're added, without re-announcing the entire history each time.
The input has an explicit aria-label since its only visible affordance is a prompt glyph, not visible label text.
Output status (success/error/info) is conveyed by both color and the resulting text content (e.g. a leading ✓ or ✗ glyph and descriptive message), not color alone.

variants.title: Terminal Command Palette
variants.description: A terminal panel with three prior commands (a status check, a successful cache clear, and a permission-denied error) and a live input line showing 'rollback' being typed with a blinking caret.
accessibility: Each output line's status is conveyed by a leading symbol and message text, not color alone.

variants.title: Terminal Command Palette (Dark)
variants.description: The same command history and input adapted to a true-black terminal surface.
accessibility: Prompt, output, and caret contrast remain legible against the true-black surface.
